_readme: Documents a human classified by hand, because no rule can honestly reach them.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The classifier in src/core/docClass.ts reaches 99.97% of Cisco's 6,117
vendor documents from evidence: Cisco's own type codes, filename markers, HTML titles and PDF
page-1 text. The residue is documents whose type nothing states - a marketing article whose
title is a phrase. Widening a rule until it swallows one document is how a classifier starts
guessing, and this project has paid for confident wrong classification twice in one day (43% of
Cisco's 'datasheets' were EoL notices; a title rule nearly promoted 4,000 distributor pages to
vendor authority). So the last few are DECIDED, by a person, with the reason written down.
An entry must carry a reason. An override with no reason is a guess with better paperwork.
Keyed by URL because doc_id is a content hash and changes when the document is revised, while
the classification of that URL does not.
If this file grows past a couple of dozen entries, that is the signal that a real rule is
missing - go and find it rather than adding another line here.

overrides.reason: Title 'Cisco CleanAir's Legacy'. A technology retrospective about the CleanAir feature, not about any orderable part: no specification tables, no PIDs. It is vendor-published long-form argument, which is what vendor_whitepaper means here. Read by hand 5 Sep 2026.
